data.reason: Under the K1 reading the main goal is on_time_deliveries, with p95_wait_s, max_wait_s and unfinished as customer monitors. Neither option's gain is robust. Option 1 raises on-time from 220.6 to 222.8 (+2.2), but only 1/5 seeds improved. Option 2 raises it from 220.6 to 222.6 (+2.0), also with only 1/5 seeds improved. In D2 I treated 2/5 seeds as too weak to act on, and I will not lower that bar now. Option 1 also overrides B and C (A ○, B ×, C ×). Its measured costs are large: B's utility falls from 73.6 to 55.0, C's from 45.4 to 28.2, and road violations rise from 23.4 to 33.6. Its customer gains are real (p95_wait_s 98.4 → 76.4, max_wait_s 146 → 128). Still, they do not justify overriding a majority vote when the main-goal gain shows on only one seed. Option 2 passed the vote and has no measured harm to customers. However, its mean gain likely comes from a single seed, and blocked s rises from 1322 to 1429. It should be measured again under next period's demand rather than adopted now. The current rules already deliver 220.6 on time, with 2.2 late, 0.0 unfinished and a lowest on-time rate of 0.98. This follows the LLM's recommendation. The vote passed option 2 only, and I decline it on the evidence. This decision also settles two open asks. K1.d.f2: no hard p95_wait_s or max_wait_s guard yet. The baselines have moved between periods (p95_wait_s 85.0 after D1, 116.4 in period 2, 98.4 now), and the KPI gives no level, so a fixed limit would be arbitrary. Any increase still counts as worse for customers, as set in K1. D1.f2: fairness stays outside the main KPI reading, as written. It remains the tie-breaker when the KPI gain is not robust, as in D2. C's utility under the current rules is 45.4, up from 19.2 after D1. Rejecting option 1 avoids a second large loss for C.
assumptions: The 5 seeds are representative of demand variation in busy periods.
The measured utilities reflect company interests accurately under fixed policies.
Keeping v2 carries no hidden deterioration beyond what the current-rules row shows.
unknowns: Whether option 2's gain holds on more seeds or under next period's demand.
How much of each option's mean gain comes from a single seed.
Whether option 1's extra road violations carry safety or third-party costs.
Why B voted against option 2 despite a small utility drop.
